newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares set for another bullish week.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares set for another bullish week.

text.p: Nigerian shares looked set to surge higher as investors with large funds continue to enter the market, dealers said after Friday's trade.
The all-share index closed at 7699.28 from 7675.89 as funds from money markets find their way into stocks which promise better yields, they said.
"Falling bank rates have been largely responsible for the growing attention shares are getting but the new funds in the market are also having an impact on the market liquidity," said one broker.
Traders said the trend would continue in the short-term, boosting stock prices.
Rising bank shares closed higher on Friday, as did petroleum marketers and manufacturing companies.
First Bank closed at a record 14.00 naira, gaining 15 kobo while Union Bank followed, closing at 12.25 naira, up 25 kobo.
Total rose by a generous 50 kobo to 70.00 naira and Unipetrol soared 30 kobo to 72.70 naira, closing as the dearest stock on the market.
Leading food companies, Cadbury closed at 32.90 naira and Nigerian Bottling Company at 43.50 naira, appreciating by 30 kobo and 50 kobo, respectively.
But giant conglomerate PZ was yet to find a level from its recent slide, finishing 50 kobo lower at 23.10 naira.
Brewer Guinness also dropped 35 kobo on big offloading to end the week at 6.75 naira.

Insurance shares made modest advances, as buyers capitalised on their relatively cheap prices. Niger Insurance added five kobo to 4.25 naira while Royal Exchange Assurance finished at 3.45 naira, up five kobo.
